answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The raven multiplier is published, charged in crystal, and sable lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1842 identities would post 3149 proofs and burn roughly 45 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
